summary: The people of an ir hanidachas, a city that was led to serve idols, have no share in Olam Haba. The mishnah explains exactly when a city gets this din, and when its people are judged one by one.

chunks.en: The people of an ir hanidachas
chunks.st: The residents of an idolatrous city

chunks.en: have no share in Olam Haba,
chunks.st: have no share in the World-to-Come,

chunks.en: as it says,
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.en: "Wicked men went out from among you
chunks.st: “Certain men, wicked persons, are gone out from your midst,

chunks.en: and led the people of their city astray."
chunks.st: and have subverted the inhabitants of their city, saying:
chunks.stMore: Let us go and let us worship other gods” (Deuteronomy 13:14).

chunks.en: And they are not killed until the ones who led them astray are

chunks.st: from that city and from that tribe,

chunks.en: And they need two witnesses and a warning for each and every one.
chunks.st: And to judge the inhabitants of a city one requires two witnesses and forewarning for each and every one who engaged in idol worship.

chunks.en: This is where single people have it harder than a crowd:
chunks.st: This is a stringency with regard to individuals who worship idols that is more stringent than the halakha with regard to multitudes who worship idols:

chunks.st: As the individuals who worship idols are executed by stoning;

chunks.en: so their property is lost.
chunks.st: their property is eliminated.

summary: Travelers staying in the city can save it from becoming an ir hanidachas. The property of the righteous people in the city is lost, but not if it is outside the city.
